doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Why schools hire performers rather than degree holders
summary: The New School wants working performers as teachers; teaching lets him be selective about gigs.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: A piece of paper or something that says here, you can do this.

Yeah. And that’s about when the time started where in some schools, especially in the east here, like well put it this way, they gave me an application to fill out just as a formal thing, and on one line it says “Degrees” but in parenthesis it says “desirable but not necessary.”
And it’s not just for the music department. I found out like most of the adjunct teachers, like in journalism or in the language department, it’s the same thing.
Right. They’ve learned it by doing it.

By doing it. And this is what they want. Because like what they said about the school, they want to turn out more performers. Because teachers, you know like take somebody that’s been to music school for four years, and this is not speaking of it negatively, but they put their four years in and get their degree. The next day they start teaching. And what do they do? They turn out more teachers. But they want people who have been out there doing it. Like in journalism most of the people weren’t teaching journalism. They worked for maybe the New York Times or the Daily News or Time/Life. And they’ve been there. They’re doing it. And this is what they want. They want to turn out more performers. Because there’s too many teachers driving cabs because there’s an overabundance.
It’s that way with performers too. We cross that bridge when we come to it.
But at least with performers you know they can go on the road.
Yeah. And many can teach part time like you do.

Yeah. And I love it. I intend to continue doing it. One thing, it’s been good for me, like especially since we got this big raise that we’re getting and all of that. It’s enabling me to be selective about the jobs I want to play, about going out of town. I don’t have to take jobs because I need the money anymore. And I’m doing two things that I like. I’m doing performing that I like and performing where I enjoy performing, and teaching, which I’ve grown to love teaching.
